prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1196; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver reporting a low-speed head-on collision in the northbound lane of a two-lane county road. Insured reports the other vehicle crossed the centerline during a passing maneuver. Insured states she was seen by a paramedic at the scene and felt neck stiffness afterward. Vehicle drivable from scene, moved to a tow yard by insured's choice. Photos requested via app.

Entry 2: Photos and damage estimate received. Front bumper cover, both headlamp assemblies, and hood show damage consistent with a low-speed impact. Airbag did not deploy in either vehicle. Police report obtained, which documents the other driver's statement that she was attempting to pass a slow truck. Liability appears to lean toward the other driver, pending witness review.

Entry 3: Contacted the other driver's carrier to open a liability claim and confirm coverage limits. Carrier acknowledged and assigned its own adjuster. Claimant on the other side has not yet been identified as represented. Sent written acknowledgment to the claimant with instructions for submitting medical records and bills.

Entry 4: Insured's passenger, a family member, reported no injuries at the scene. Claimant has reported neck strain to the insured and has told the carrier she saw her primary care provider and is attending physical therapy twice weekly. Requested medical authorization form and itemized bills. Claimant has not retained an attorney to my knowledge and has been responsive to phone calls.

Entry 5: Reviewed rental coverage and confirmed the insured has a rental car through her policy. Estimate on repairs reviewed and approved for shop. Reserve set based on preliminary medical information and vehicle damage. Diary set for follow-up once medical records arrive and once the carrier responds on liability.
